title: Bronco Racing FSAE Electric
subtitle: High-voltage systems for SCU's first electric formula cars
pitch: High-voltage electrical work on Santa Clara University's Formula SAE Electric cars: BR1, the team's first electric formula car, and BR2, an all-new design for June 2027.
highlights: Programmed, configured, and modified the Orion BMS 2 for a 420 V max accumulator
Hand-soldered a custom harness of 140+ thermistors
Placement optimization improved thermal-measurement accuracy by about 50 percent, as measured
Architected the vehicle CAN bus and wrote the STM32 acquisition firmware
Installed and programmed the 540 V on-board charger and designed the charging cart
BR2 design: 120s4p of Molicel P50B cells, 504 V max

blocks.md: BR1 is SCU's first electric formula car. I joined Bronco Racing in September 2023 as an Electrical Specialist and served as High-Voltage & Co-Electrical Lead for BR1 from November 2025 to June 2026.

rows.label: Voltage
rows.value: About 360 V nominal, about 420 V max

rows.label: BMS

blocks.heading: What I did on BR1
items: Programmed the Orion BMS 2: cell-voltage monitoring, temperature sensing, state-of-charge algorithms, and safety-interlock logic, bench-validated to the FSAE EV rules.
Designed thermal-management expansion modules for the Orion BMS 2.
Designed the accumulator wiring architecture and the thermistor-placement strategy, then soldered the 140+ thermistor harness by hand.
Co-designed the shutdown and charging-shutdown circuits with the team and caught protection-logic errors before fabrication.
Reviewed the precharge, discharge, and IMD board designs for FSAE EV compliance.
Architected the vehicle CAN bus and wrote STM32 firmware for real-time sensor interfacing, data logging, and custom diagnostics.
Built a Python GUI for live CAN monitoring and automated diagnostics on the thermal-management subsystem.
Installed and programmed the 540 V on-board charger and created the charging safety protocols.
Designed the charging cart with current and voltage control, a safety-shutdown circuit, and a deadman lock.
Led team training on precision soldering, thermal-system architecture, and HV safety.

blocks.md: The team took BR1 to competition in June 2026 and completed the static events. The high-voltage system was designed, built, programmed, and bench-validated. It was not energized at competition, a deliberate safety call.

BR2 is an all-new design. As Electrical System Officer (ESO) & HV Engineer, I work with the team across the electrical and tractive-system stack. Design and ordering started in summer 2026, the build is targeted for March and April 2027, and competition is June 2027. Our working model is rules-first: every design decision is traced to a cited FSAE rule.

rows.label: Accumulator design
rows.value: 120s4p of Molicel P50B 21700 cells, 480 cells in all
